report:
-Date of report: 2026-09-18
-Name of stock: Jubilee Metals Group (JBL.JO)
-Current price: ZAR 0.45
-Exchange rate assumptions: USDZAR 16.4059
-Commodity assumptions: Copper US$13,690.71 per tonne (US$6.21 per lb)
-Report target price: ZAR 1.70
-Positive risks (upside):
Imminent conclusion of due diligence on the US$35.0 million Large Waste Project sale releasing a US$2.25 million deposit.
Ramp-up of Molefe Mine feed to 7,500 tonnes per month in October 2026 and 10,000 tonnes per month by end-CY2026, supported by upcoming Phase 2 drilling results.
Stable-state operations at Roan Concentrator providing clear FY2027 guidance of 2,850 to 3,150 tonnes of copper units following the commissioning of the dewatering circuit.
-Negative risks (downside):
Acute input cost inflation in Zambia with domestic acid costs rising over 200 percent and diesel costs increasing 90 percent during Q4 FY2026.
Operational complexity and potential bottlenecks from executing 1.14 million tonnes of remaining pre-stripping in parallel with active reef mining at Molefe.
Counterparty execution risk regarding the final transaction agreements and staged instalment payments for the US$35.0 million asset disposal.

1 Investment Thesis

Jubilee Metals Group remains a Buy. The investment case is supported by significant operational expansion in Zambia and the imminent monetisation of non-core assets. FY2026 operational results confirmed a 225 percent year-on-year increase in combined mine and concentrator copper production to 3,739 tonnes. The Roan Concentrator has reached operational maturity and stable-state guidance of 2,850 to 3,150 tonnes of copper for FY2027, backed by the newly commissioned fines dewatering circuit. 

The strategic disposal of the Large Waste Project for US$35.0 million (approximately ZAR 574.2 million) is approaching due diligence completion, which will trigger an exclusivity deposit of US$2.25 million. This capital provides non-dilutive liquidity to fund the expansion of Jubilee-controlled mining assets, specifically the Molefe Mine open-pit and the upcoming Project G development slated for February 2027. Despite severe temporary acid and diesel cost inflation in Zambia during Q4 FY2026, the vertical integration into self-mined ore will improve refinery feed stability and operating margins. Following the share price pullback to ZAR 0.45, the stock offers an asymmetric risk-to-reward profile.

2 Key Operational Metrics

Annualized Units Produced: 12,000 tonnes copper

All-in Sustaining Cost (AISC): US$5,950 per tonne

Weighted Average Shares in Issue: 3,146,295,996

Effective Tax Rate: 27%

Valuation Methods used: Sum-of-the-Parts (SOTP) and DCF. Key assumptions:

Growth rate: 5%

Discount rate (WACC): 12%

Exit multiple: 6.0x

12-month target price: ZAR 1.70

Implied upside/downside: 277.8%

3 Spot HEPS Equation

Equation format: HEPS = [(Spot Price - AISC) * Production * (1 - Tax Rate)] / Shares

Variable A (AISC used): 5,950

Variable B (Production used): 12,000

Variable C (Tax/Shares factor): 0.00000000023202

Example Calculation:
Using current commodity price of US$13,690.71 per tonne (US$6.21 per lb):
HEPS = [(13,690.71 - 5,950) * 12,000 * 0.73] / 3,146,295,996
HEPS = US$0.021552 per share
Converted to ZAR @ 16.4059 = ZARc 35.36 per share

4 Detailed Positive Risks / Upside Catalysts

Non-dilutive Liquidity: Completion of due diligence on the Large Waste Project transaction within the coming week will secure an initial US$2.25 million deposit and unlock up to US$35.0 million in staged capital (or US$30.0 million accelerated settlement). This funds Zambian mining growth without shareholder dilution.

Molefe Mine Expansion: Dispatching high-grade ROM to Sable is set to step up to 7,500 tonnes per month in October 2026 and targeted to reach 10,000 tonnes per month before end-CY2026. Phase 2 drilling results due within two weeks and a JORC-compliant resource statement in Q4 CY2026 will provide formal resource validation.

Process Debottlenecking: The installation of the Roan concentrate dewatering circuit enables the conversion of built-up oxide fines inventory (913 tonnes of contained copper) into refinery feed, enhancing volume output and cash generation in FY2027.

5 Detailed Negative Risks / Key Uncertainties

Input Cost Inflation: In Q4 FY2026, Zambian domestic acid availability tightened severely, driving acid prices up by more than 200 percent, while diesel prices rose 90 percent. Sustained elevated reagent and energy costs could compress refinery margins and elevate group AISC.

Mine Plan Execution: The updated Molefe plan requires 1.6 million tonnes of pre-stripping, of which 1.14 million tonnes remain to be completed in parallel with active reef mining. Operational interruptions or adverse strip ratios could slow ROM delivery to Sable.

Transaction Finalisation: The sale of the Large Waste Project remains subject to final transaction agreements following due diligence. Any delays or disputes regarding contract execution or instalment payments would impact forecast cash inflows.

6 Conclusion

BUY rating maintained with a total expected return of 277.8 percent.

Summary of Changes

Financials: Target price maintained at ZAR 1.70. With the share price declining from ZAR 0.60 to ZAR 0.45, implied upside expanded from 183.3 percent to 277.8 percent. Commodity assumptions updated to Copper US$13,690.71 per tonne (US$6.21 per lb) and USDZAR to 16.4059, adjusting Spot HEPS from ZARc 35.04 to ZARc 35.36.

Outlook: Reaffirmed Buy conviction. FY2026 production confirmed a 225 percent surge in pre-refining copper output to 3,739 tonnes. Roan has achieved stable-state operations with FY2027 production guided at 2,850 to 3,150 tonnes of copper.

Risks: Incorporated acute local cost pressures from acid costs rising over 200 percent and diesel increasing 90 percent during Q4 FY2026. Highlighted execution risks associated with parallel open-pit pre-stripping at Molefe.

Developments: Large Waste Project due diligence is concluding within a week to unlock a US$2.25 million exclusivity deposit. Fines concentrate dewatering circuit commissioned at Roan. Phase 2 drill results for Molefe expected within two weeks ahead of the Q4 CY2026 JORC resource statement. Project G development scheduled to commence in February 2027.
